title: Snails and Slugs
objective: After this level you can describe snails, slugs and their relatives.
summary: Snails and slugs are gastropods, the largest mollusk group. They glide on one muscular foot over mucus and eat with a radula of tiny teeth. Slugs lost their shells.

cards.headline: A slug is a snail that lost its shell.
cards.body: Not in an accident: over the course of evolution. In slugs, the shell has shrunk to a small leftover inside the body, or vanished completely. Snails and slugs are the same kind of animal, a gastropod, and they share some very strange equipment.

cards.headline: Meet the mollusks
cards.body: Snails and slugs are mollusks: soft-bodied invertebrates, usually wrapped wholly or partly in a shell made by a layer of tissue called the mantle. Gastropods, the snails and slugs, are the largest group of mollusks. Their relatives include clams, mussels and oysters, and also squids and octopuses. A garden snail and a squid are family, which shows how much you can do with “soft-bodied.”

cards.headline: Life on one foot
cards.body: A snail travels on its foot, a single muscular organ that ripples with waves of contraction. Land snails and slugs glide along on a track of mucus. That shiny trail across your garden path is the road a snail builds for itself as it goes.

cards.fact: A snail eats with a ribbon of teeth.
cards.context: Snails and slugs eat with a jaw and a radula, a flexible band of thousands of microscopic teeth. The jaw cuts off a piece of leaf, and the radula rasps it down; covered in rows of tiny teeth, it’s coarse like sandpaper. So when a snail eats your lettuce, it isn’t biting it. It’s sanding it.

mascot.line: Thousands of teeth and not one toothbrush. Snails really commit to the salad.

cards.headline: Snails and slugs: sorted
learned: Snails and slugs are gastropods, a kind of mollusk
Mollusks: soft bodies, shells made by the mantle
One muscular foot, gliding on mucus
A radula: thousands of tiny teeth

questions.prompt: What does a snail use to rasp its food?

options.label: A radula, a band of tiny teeth
Two pairs of antennae
options.rationale: Those are crustacean feelers, not a snail’s eating tool.

questions.explanation: Snails and slugs eat with a jaw and a radula, a flexible band of thousands of microscopic teeth.

questions.prompt: How is a slug related to a snail?

options.label: It’s a snail that crawled out of its shell
options.rationale: A snail can’t leave its shell; slugs lost theirs over evolution.

options.label: It’s a gastropod whose shell shrank or vanished
It’s a worm that lives like a snail
It’s a young snail before its shell grows
options.rationale: Slugs are adults of their own kinds.

questions.explanation: Slugs are gastropods whose shells were reduced to an internal fragment or lost over evolution.

questions.prompt: Level 3 said most mollusks wear a hard outer skeleton. Where does a snail’s shell come from?

options.label: It’s hardened mucus from its trail
options.rationale: Mucus is for gliding, not building.

options.label: It forms from swallowed sand
options.rationale: The shell is made by the body itself.

options.label: The mantle, a layer of tissue, makes it

questions.explanation: A mollusk’s shell is secreted by the mantle, a layer of tissue covering the body.
